question: does behavioural dedup lose front membership because its members are worse, or because the rejected-candidate amortisation divides the same search work over far fewer retained members?
statement: the 200-of-200 sweep on FULL burden is largely an accounting consequence: amortising the same search work over far fewer retained members inflates every dedup record's burden by about the same factor, and retaining fewer members is precisely what dedup does. With the rejected-candidate term removed, no-dedup still wins more often but does not sweep. The residual difference is real -- no-dedup members carry lower own-lifetime burden -- and is explained by the within-class burden spread.
what_is_still_claimed: no-dedup retains cheaper organisms at equal n on own-lifetime burden, and the mechanism is that keeping the first-encountered member of a behaviour class discards alternatives averaging 93.7% cheaper
what_is_withdrawn: that the 200-of-200 result on full burden demonstrates behavioural dedup selects worse organisms; on full burden it mostly demonstrates that dedup retains fewer of them
